questions.q: Escalator standby mode—maximum inactivity
questions.n: Standard regulations specify 5 minutes of inactivity before an escalator enters standby mode to conserve energy.

questions.q: Elevator lighting shuts off after inactivity for maximum of:
questions.n: Current energy codes require elevator car lighting to deactivate after a maximum of 3 minutes of idle time.

questions.q: Elevator energy efficient lighting and display lighting in the elevator car shall have an average lamp efficacy of:
questions.n: 55 lumens per watt is the required average efficacy to ensure energy-efficient illumination within the car.

questions.q: Elevator lighting shall switch off after the elevator has been inactive for a maximum period of:
questions.n: The maximum period defined for this specific lighting deactivation requirement is 5 minutes.

questions.q: Elevated Water Storage: Percentage for fire reserve over and above the average daily demand supply.
questions.n: Codes require a 20% additional capacity specifically dedicated to fire protection beyond daily domestic use.

questions.q: Elevated Water Storage: Minimum buildings storeys high are exempt from Elevated Water Storage provision.
questions.n: Buildings up to 10 storeys high are specified as the threshold for exemption from these particular storage provisions.

questions.q: WATER FIXTURES: Maximum Flow Rate Dual Flush Water Closet
questions.n: The standard maximum for dual flush systems is 3 liters for a half flush and 6 liters for a full flush.

questions.q: WATER FIXTURES: Maximum Flow Rate Single Flush Water Closet
questions.n: 4.9 liters is the maximum allowable volume for a single flush to be considered water-efficient.

questions.q: WATER FIXTURES: Maximum Flow Rate Shower
questions.n: The maximum permissible flow rate for showerheads to meet conservation standards is 9 liters per minute.

questions.q: WATER FIXTURES: Maximum Flow Rate Urinals
questions.n: Modern efficiency codes limit urinal flush volume to a maximum of 1 liter per flush.

questions.q: WATER FIXTURES: Maximum Flow Rate Lavatory taps
questions.n: The maximum flow rate for lavatory (bathroom sink) taps is set at 4.8 liters per minute.

questions.q: WATER FIXTURES: Maximum Flow Rate Kitchen faucets
questions.n: Standard efficiency requirements for kitchen faucets allow for a maximum of 4.8 liters per minute.

questions.q: WATER FIXTURES: Maximum Flow Rate Handheld bidet sprays
questions.n: Handheld bidet sprays are regulated to the same 4.8 liters per minute maximum as other taps.

questions.q: Rainwater Harvesting: Minimum storage tanks size (in cu.m) shall be calculated by dividing the building footprint area by...
questions.n: The standard calculation for minimum rainwater tank volume is the building footprint area divided by 75.

questions.q: Open Space Utilization: A minimum of __________ of the required Unpaved Surface Area (USA), as required in Rule VII and VIII of the NBC, shall be vegetated with indigenous and adaptable species.
questions.n: The National Building Code requires that at least half (50%) of the unpaved surface area be vegetated.

questions.q: Average LPD (W/m2) for Residential Dwelling: Condominium
questions.n: The Lighting Power Density (LPD) limit for residential condominiums is set at 10.8 W/m².

questions.q: Average LPD (W/m2) for Hotel / Resort
questions.n: Hotels and resorts share the same 10.8 W/m² Lighting Power Density limit as condominiums and offices.

questions.q: Average LPD (W/m2) for Educational: School
questions.n: Educational facilities like schools are permitted an LPD of 12.9 W/m² to ensure adequate lighting for learning.

questions.q: Average LPD (W/m2) for Institutional: Hospital
questions.n: Hospitals and other institutional buildings have an LPD limit of 12.9 W/m².

questions.q: Average LPD (W/m2) for Business: Office
questions.n: Business offices are restricted to a Lighting Power Density of 10.8 W/m².

questions.q: Average LPD (W/m2) for Mercantile: Mall - (excluding accent lighting)
questions.n: Malls (Mercantile) are allowed a higher LPD of 16.1 W/m² for general area lighting.

questions.q: Average LPD (W/m2) for Covered parking
questions.n: Covered parking structures are allowed a Lighting Power Density of 3.2 W/m².

questions.q: Average LPD (W/m2) for Open and outdoor parking
questions.n: Open and outdoor parking areas have an LPD limit of 1.6 W/m².

questions.q: Average LPD (W/m2) for Exterior Façade
questions.n: Exterior façade lighting is limited to a Lighting Power Density of 2.15 W/m².

questions.q: Average LPD (W/m2) for Active entrance (pedestrian conveyance)
questions.n: Active entrances for pedestrian conveyance have a high LPD limit of 98.4 W/m² for safety and visibility.

questions.q: Average LPD (W/m2) for Inactive entrance (normally locked / inactive use)
questions.n: Inactive or normally locked entrances have an LPD limit of 65.6 W/m².

questions.q: What is the prevailing wind in the Philippines from November to April, coming from a North-Easterly direction?
questions.n: Amihan is the Northeast monsoon, bringing cooler, dry air from November to April.

questions.q: What is the prevailing wind in the Philippines from May to October, coming from a South-Westerly direction?
questions.n: Habagat is the Southwest monsoon, typically bringing warm and rainy weather between May and October.

questions.q: What is the process of supplying air to and removing air from an indoor space without using mechanical systems?
questions.n: Natural ventilation relies on pressure differences and wind to move air without fans or blowers.

questions.q: What passive cooling technique relies on air entering through one side of a room and exiting through another to create airflow?
questions.n: Cross ventilation occurs when openings on opposite or adjacent walls allow wind to flow through a space.

questions.q: What phenomenon occurs when air is forced through a narrow opening, causing an increase in wind speed and a drop in pressure?
questions.n: The Venturi Effect describes how wind accelerates as it is squeezed through narrow gaps or openings.

questions.q: What effect uses the buoyancy of warm air to pull cooler air in from lower openings, often utilized in high-ceiling structures?
questions.n: Warm air rises (buoyancy), creating a vacuum that draws cooler air in from below, like a chimney.

questions.q: What term describes the variation in wind speed at different heights above the ground?
questions.n: Wind gradient describes how wind speed increases as you move higher above the earth's surface.

questions.q: Which type of sun-shading device is most effective for South-facing windows to block high-altitude summer sun?
questions.n: Horizontal devices (like overhangs) effectively block the high-noon sun typical of South-facing exposures.

questions.q: Which type of sun-shading device is most effective for East and West-facing windows to block low-angle morning or afternoon sun?
questions.n: Vertical fins are best for blocking low-angle sun coming from the sides (East and West).

questions.q: What shading device combines both horizontal and vertical elements to form a grid?
questions.n: An egg crate combines horizontal and vertical fins to provide comprehensive shading from multiple angles.

questions.q: What design philosophy focuses on local climate to provide thermal and visual comfort using environmental resources like the sun and wind?
questions.n: Bioclimatic design uses local environmental conditions to naturally maintain building comfort.

questions.q: What are the primary advantages of Bioclimatic Design?
o: Reduced energy consumption, lower utility costs, improved indoor air quality, and enhanced occupant comfort.
Use of high-tech mechanical systems and smart sensors.
Lower initial material costs and structural simplicity.
Aesthetic appeal and faster construction speed.
questions.n: These factors represent the core benefits of using natural forces for building regulation.

questions.q: What type of glass has a microscopically thin coating that reflects infrared energy (heat) while letting visible light pass through?
questions.n: Low-E glass coatings minimize the amount of ultraviolet and infrared light that can pass through glass.

questions.q: What glazing system consists of two panes of glass separated by a vacuum or gas-filled space to reduce heat transfer?
questions.n: Double glazing creates an insulating air/gas pocket between two panes to slow heat flow.

questions.q: What is a cost-effective way to improve the solar performance of existing windows without replacing the entire pane?
questions.n: Solar control films can be applied to existing glass to reflect heat and UV rays economically.

questions.q: What metric measures the ratio of the total area of a building facade occupied by windows to the total facade area?
questions.n: WWR is a key metric in building design to balance daylighting with thermal gain.

questions.q: In building orientation, which side of a building typically receives the most intense solar heat gain in a tropical climate?
questions.n: The West facade receives intense afternoon sun when the ambient air temperature is already at its peak.

questions.q: What value measures the capacity of a material to resist heat flow?
questions.n: The R-value indicates the thermal resistance of a material; higher values mean better insulation.

questions.q: What common type of insulation comes in rolls or batts, usually made of fiberglass or mineral wool?
questions.n: Blanket insulation consists of flexible fibers, commonly fiberglass, packaged in rolls or batts.

questions.q: What insulation type consists of pre-formed boards of plastic foam, providing high thermal resistance in a thin profile?
questions.n: Rigid foam boards (like EPS or XPS) offer high R-values per inch of thickness.

questions.q: What system uses interlocking modular units filled with concrete to provide both structure and high insulation?
questions.n: ICF systems use stay-in-place foam forms that are filled with concrete to create insulated walls.

questions.q: What insulation method involves blowing cellulose or glass fibers into wall cavities or attics?
questions.n: This method uses a machine to distribute loose particles of insulation into hard-to-reach areas.

questions.q: What material is designed to reflect thermal radiation and is usually installed in attics to reduce summer heat gain?
questions.n: Radiant barriers (often foil-faced) reflect radiant heat away from the building interior.

questions.q: What high-performance building component consists of an insulating foam core sandwiched between two structural facings?
questions.n: SIPs provide both structural support and insulation in one integrated factory-built unit.
